builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Safe Resemblance, Silent Propagation: Limits of Text-Similarity Guardrails for AI Agent Safety
summary: The paper argues that text-similarity guardrails like DonkeyRail fail to distinguish between malicious instruction propagation and legitimate quotation in AI agent communications. The method replaces behavioral analysis with surface-level text matching, requiring continuous calibration and producing high false positive rates that vary across different templates and use cases. The approach fails when identical visible transcripts require different safety decisions based on governing policies, which observation-only classifiers cannot resolve.
rationale: The technique demonstrates fundamental flaws in existing text-similarity approaches for AI safety and is not directly implementable as a production solution, but rather identifies why current methods fail.
technique: Text-similarity guardrails for AI agent safety

claims.statement: The paper argues that text-similarity guardrails like DonkeyRail fail to distinguish between malicious instruction propagation and legitimate quotation in AI agent communications. The method replaces behavioral analysis with surface-level text matching, requiring continuous calibration and producing high false positive rates that vary across different templates and use cases. The approach fails when identical visible transcripts require different safety decisions based on governing policies, which observation-only classifiers cannot resolve.

The study demonstrates that DonkeyRail misses 8 of 19 functional outputs while flagging 70 of 192 legitimate replies at default threshold, with every completed quotation and template-reuse reply triggering false alerts.
